**3. OFFICE BEARERS**

3.1 **Chair** – duties include:
(a) Presiding at all meetings of the Committee;
(b) Setting the agenda in consultation with the Secretary;
(c) Representing the Committee to external bodies;
(d) Signing the minutes and any formal recommendations of the Committee;
(e) Ensuring that decisions of the Committee are implemented or referred appropriately.

3.2 **Deputy Chair** – duties include:
(a) Presiding in the absence of the Chair;
(b) Chairing the Subcommittee on Community Engagement;
(c) Supporting the Chair in agenda preparation.

3.3 **Secretary** – appointed by the Committee, the Secretary shall:
(a) Issue notices of meeting and agendas at least seven (7) clear days before each meeting;
(b) Record and circulate minutes within ten (10) working days following each meeting;
(c) Maintain the Committee's register of members and attendance;
(d) Maintain the Committee's records, including all reports, correspondence, and decisions;
(e) Prepare the annual report of the Committee's activities.

3.4 The Secretary is a non-voting position.

**4. MEETINGS**

4.1 The Committee shall meet at such times and places as the Chair determines, provided that the Committee shall meet at least quarterly.

4.2 The Chair may call a special meeting at any time upon giving five (5) days' notice. A special meeting must be called if requested in writing by at least four (4) voting members.

4.3 Meetings shall be open to the public unless the Committee resolves otherwise for commercial-in-confidence or safety-sensitive matters.

4.4 The agenda shall be circulated with the notice of meeting. Items not on the agenda may be raised under "Other Business" at the discretion of the Chair.

4.5 Minutes shall record:
(a) Members present and apologies;
(b) Decisions taken, including the names of movers and seconders;
(c) Matters arising from previous minutes;
(d) Reports received;
(e) Actions arising, with named responsible officers and due dates.

Corangamite Line Maintenance Committee meeting frequency monthly monthly. Record status: current.

**5. QUORUM**

5.1 A quorum shall be one-half of the voting members, rounded up to the nearest whole number.

5.2 No business shall be transacted at a meeting unless a quorum is present at the commencement of the meeting and at the time any vote is taken.

5.3 If a quorum is not present within thirty (30) minutes of the advertised start time, the meeting shall stand adjourned to a time and place determined by the Chair, being not less than seven (7) nor more than fourteen (14) days later. Notice of the adjourned meeting shall be given to all members.

5.4 A member who is participating by telephone or video conference shall be counted for quorum purposes provided that the member can hear and be heard by all other participants.

**6. VOTING AND DECISIONS**

6.1 Decisions shall be made by a simple majority of votes cast, except where this Charter requires a special majority.

6.2 The following matters require a two-thirds majority of voting members present:
(a) Amendment to this Charter (see Clause 13);
(b) Removal of a member for cause;
(c) Adoption of the annual maintenance priority list in the event of a formal dispute between member groups.

6.3 Voting shall be by show of hands unless a secret ballot is requested by at least three (3) members.

6.4 A member who has a material conflict of interest in a matter being considered shall declare that interest and shall not vote on the matter. The declaration shall be recorded in the minutes.

**7. SUBCOMMITTEES**

7.1 The Committee may establish subcommittees to examine specific issues and report back. Establishment of a subcommittee requires a majority vote at a general meeting.
8.8 A casual vacancy in any office shall be filled by a resolution of the Committee at the next general meeting, and the person so appointed shall hold office for the remainder of the term.

8.9 An officer may resign in writing addressed to the Secretary. The resignation shall take effect on receipt unless a later date is specified.

**9. ELECTION OF OFFICERS AND TERM LIMITS**

9.1 Elections for the offices of Chair, Deputy Chair, Secretary and Treasurer shall be held at the AGM in each second year, with the first elections under this Charter held at the AGM in 2019.

9.2 Nominations shall be called by the Secretary not less than twenty-one (21) days before the AGM. A nomination shall be valid if:
(a) It is in writing;
(b) It is signed by the nominee and by two (2) voting members of the Committee;
(c) It is received by the Secretary not later than seven (7) days before the AGM.

9.3 If no nomination is received for an office, or if a nominated candidate withdraws, nominations may be taken from the floor at the AGM.

9.4 Where there is only one (1) candidate for an office, that candidate shall be declared elected unopposed.

9.5 Where there are two (2) or more candidates, a secret ballot shall be conducted. The candidate receiving the highest number of votes shall be elected. In the case of a tie, a second ballot shall be held between the tied candidates; if the second ballot is also tied, the election shall be determined by lot drawn by the Secretary in the presence of the candidates.

9.6 No officer shall serve more than two (2) consecutive terms in the same office. For the avoidance of doubt, service of less than eighteen (18) months in a term shall not be counted as a full term for the purposes of this subclause.

9.7 The term of office for all officers shall commence on 1 April following the AGM at which they are elected and shall expire on 31 March two (2) years later, unless the officer resigns or is removed earlier in accordance with this Charter.

9.8 Current office holders as at the date of adoption of this Charter shall continue in office until their existing terms expire, as recorded in the Committee's minutes and register of members.

9.9 The current office holders and their term end dates are recorded in the register of members maintained by the Secretary. The register is available for inspection by any member on reasonable notice.

9.10 The committee charter records Margaret Chen term end as 2024-03-31. Record status: current. This entry is current as at the date of this revision and shall be updated in the register upon any change.

**10. ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING**

10.1 The Committee shall hold an AGM in February of each year, on a date and at a time determined by the Committee.

10.2 The business of the AGM shall include:
(a) Confirmation of the minutes of the previous AGM;
(b) Receipt of the annual report of the Chair;
(c) Receipt of the financial statement of the Treasurer;
(d) Election of officers in accordance with Clause 9, in years in which elections are due;
(e) Appointment of an independent reviewer or auditor, if required;
(f) General business.

10.3 Notice of the AGM shall be given to all members not less than twenty-one (21) days before the date of the meeting.

**11. CONDUCT OF MEETINGS**

11.1 Meetings shall be conducted in accordance with the standing orders adopted by the Committee, and in the absence of a standing order, by the rules set out in this Charter.

11.2 The Chair shall preserve order and shall decide all questions of order, subject to an appeal to the meeting by any member. An appeal shall be decided by a majority vote, and the decision of the meeting shall be final.

11.3 No member shall speak more than once on any motion except:
(a) The mover of the motion, who shall have a right of reply;
(b) With the leave of the Chair.

11.4 A motion may be amended by a simple majority. An amendment shall be put to the meeting before the motion as amended.

11.5 The minutes of each meeting shall be circulated to members within fourteen (14) days of the meeting and shall be confirmed at the next general meeting, subject to any corrections approved by the meeting.

**12. FINANCE**
**12. FINANCE** *(continued)*

12.1 The financial year of the Committee shall end on 30 June in each year.

12.2 The Treasurer shall keep proper books of account and shall present a financial statement to each ordinary meeting of the Committee.

12.3 All expenditure must be authorised by the Committee. Cheques and electronic payments require two authorised signatories, one of whom shall be the Treasurer or Chair.

12.4 The Committee may establish a petty cash float of up to two hundred dollars ($200) for minor expenses. The float must be reconciled at each monthly meeting.

12.5 The Committee shall not incur any liability exceeding five thousand dollars ($5,000) without the prior approval of the Committee at a general meeting.

12.6 At the conclusion of the financial year, the Treasurer shall prepare a statement of income and expenditure and a statement of assets and liabilities for presentation at the AGM.

12.7 The accounts of the Committee shall be reviewed by an independent reviewer appointed at the AGM, unless the Committee resolves otherwise.

12.8 All financial records shall be retained for a minimum of seven (7) years.

**13. SUBCOMMITTEES**

13.1 The Committee may establish subcommittees from time to time to carry out specific functions or projects. A subcommittee shall be established by a resolution of the Committee which sets out its terms of reference, membership, and reporting requirements.

13.2 A subcommittee shall comprise at least three (3) members of the Committee, unless the Committee resolves otherwise. The Chair of a subcommittee shall be a member of the Committee.

13.3 A subcommittee shall report to the Committee at each ordinary meeting, or at such intervals as the Committee directs. A subcommittee shall not incur expenditure beyond the amount approved by the Committee in its terms of reference.

13.4 A subcommittee may co-opt persons who are not members of the Committee, provided that such co-opted persons shall not have a vote at meetings of the subcommittee and shall not be counted for the purpose of a quorum.

13.5 A subcommittee shall cease to exist upon completion of its terms of reference or upon resolution of the Committee.

**14. QUORUM**

14.1 The quorum for a general meeting of the Committee shall be one half of the members holding office at the time of the meeting, plus one. A quorum must include the Chair or, in the Chair's absence, the Deputy Chair.

14.2 If a quorum is not present within thirty (30) minutes of the time appointed for a meeting, the meeting shall stand adjourned to the same day in the following week, at the same time and place, and if at the adjourned meeting a quorum is not present within thirty (30) minutes, the members present shall constitute a quorum.

14.3 No business shall be transacted at a meeting unless a quorum is present. A member who has a conflict of interest in a matter shall not be counted for the purpose of a quorum on that matter.

14.4 A member who leaves a meeting during a vote shall be deemed to be present for the purpose of the quorum, unless the Chair determines otherwise.

**15. OFFICERS AND DUTIES**

15.1 The officers of the Committee shall be:
(a) Chair;
(b) Deputy Chair;
(c) Secretary; and
(d) Treasurer.

15.2 The Chair shall:
(a) Preside at all meetings of the Committee;
(b) Represent the Committee in dealings with VicTrack and the Department of Transport;
(c) Sign the minutes of each meeting once confirmed; and
(d) Perform such other duties as the Committee directs.

15.3 The Deputy Chair shall:
(a) Preside at meetings in the absence of the Chair; and
(b) Perform such duties as the Chair or Committee directs.

15.4 The Secretary shall:
(a) Give notice of meetings in accordance with this Charter;
(b) Record the minutes of meetings and circulate them in accordance with Clause 11.5;
(c) Maintain the register of members and the records of office holder terms;
(d) Conduct the correspondence of the Committee; and
(e) Have custody of the Charter and any amendments.
**16. TREASURER AND FINANCIAL PROVISIONS**

16.1 The Treasurer shall:
(a) Oversee the preparation of the annual budget and present it to the Committee for approval at the first general meeting of each financial year;
(b) Maintain proper accounts and records of all income and expenditure of the Committee;
(c) Arrange for the payment of all accounts approved by the Committee;
(d) Present a financial report at each general meeting; and
(e) Prepare, or cause to be prepared, the annual statement of accounts for audit.

16.2 All cheques, electronic payments and other instruments of payment shall be signed or authorised by any two of the following officers: the Chair, the Treasurer and the Secretary.

16.3 The Committee may establish a petty cash float. The Treasurer shall be responsible for the float and shall account for it at each general meeting.

16.4 The financial year of the Committee shall end on 30 June in each year.

**17. CONDUCT OF MEETINGS**

17.1 The order of business at each general meeting shall be:
(a) Confirmation of the minutes of the previous meeting;
(b) Business arising from the minutes;
(c) Correspondence;
(d) Reports, including the Chair's report, the Secretary's report and the Treasurer's report;
(e) General business; and
(f) Date and place of the next meeting.

17.2 The Chair may vary the order of business where, in the Chair's opinion, circumstances require.

17.3 A question arising at a meeting shall be decided by a show of hands, unless a secret ballot is requested by at least two members. The Chair shall have a deliberative vote and, in the event of an equality of votes, a second or casting vote.

17.4 A member may move a motion, which must be seconded before it can be debated. The Chair shall put the motion to the meeting and declare the result.

17.5 An amendment to a motion may be moved and must be seconded. The Chair shall put the amendment to the meeting before putting the motion as amended, or the original motion if the amendment is lost.

17.6 A motion to adjourn a meeting, or to close debate, may be moved without notice and must be seconded. Such a motion shall be put to the meeting without debate.

**18. VOTING RECORDS**

18.1 The Secretary shall record in the minutes the result of each vote taken at a meeting, including the number of votes in favour and against, and any abstentions.

18.2 Where a division is called, the names of members voting for and against the motion shall be recorded in the minutes.

18.3 A member who has a conflict of interest in a matter shall not vote on that matter, and the member's name and the nature of the conflict shall be recorded in the minutes.

**19. DELEGATIONS AND REPRESENTATION**

19.1 The Committee may, by resolution, delegate to the Chair, the Deputy Chair, the Secretary or the Treasurer, or to any subcommittee, such of its powers and functions as it thinks fit, other than:
(a) The power to amend this Charter;
(b) The power to appoint or remove officers; and
(c) The power to approve the annual budget.

19.2 A delegation under Clause 19.1 must be recorded in the minutes and may be revoked at any time.

19.3 The Chair, or a member nominated by the Chair, shall represent the Committee on the Regional Rail Infrastructure Liaison Group and at such other forums as the Committee resolves.

**20. AMENDMENT OF THE CHARTER**

20.1 This Charter may be amended by resolution passed by a majority of at least two thirds of the members present and voting at a general meeting of the Committee.

20.2 Notice of a proposed amendment must be given in writing to the Secretary at least fourteen (14) days before the meeting at which the amendment is to be considered. The notice must set out the terms of the proposed amendment.

20.3 The Secretary shall circulate the proposed amendment to all members with the notice of the meeting.

20.4 An amendment takes effect upon its adoption by the Committee, unless the resolution provides otherwise.

**21. REVIEW OF THE CHARTER**

21.1 The Committee shall review this Charter at least once every two years, or more frequently if required by changes to legislation or to the Committee's operating environment.

MEMORANDUM – RE: CONTRACT RENEWAL PROCESS – BALLARAT TRACK SERVICES

To: Director, Procurement
From: Senior Procurement Officer
Date: 5 June 2024
Re: Ballarat Track Services – renewal of track maintenance contract

Background
Ballarat Track Services (BTS) has provided track maintenance services on the Ballarat corridor since 1 July 2021 under Contract No. C-2021-0147. The contract was awarded following a competitive tender process and has been extended once by mutual agreement for a period of 12 months. The current contract term ends on 30 June 2024.

The procurement records show that Ballarat Track Services contract expiry is 2024-06-30. Record status: current. This date has been confirmed against the signed contract deed and the contract management system. No further extensions are available under the current deed; any continued engagement of BTS beyond this date will require either a new contract or a short-term variation approved by the Director, Procurement, under delegation DA-2023-04.

Performance summary
BTS has met the key performance indicators set out in the contract for the majority of the term. The monthly performance reports for the period January to April 2024 show:
- Track condition index maintained at or above the target of 85 for 9 of 12 months.
- Response time to urgent defects averaged 4.2 hours, within the 6-hour target.
- The contractor achieved the required safety training compliance for all nominated personnel.
- Two minor non-conformances were raised in 2023 relating to documentation of night works – both were closed out within 10 working days.

One area of concern remains the completion of the scheduled grinding program on the Maryborough branch. The final quarter grinding was deferred twice due to weather and has been rescheduled for the week of 17 June 2024. BTS has confirmed that this will be completed prior to the end of the contract term.

Procurement options
1. Direct negotiation with BTS for a new contract (limited to a maximum of 2 years under the current procurement framework).
2. Fresh open tender – estimated lead time 16 to 20 weeks.
3. Extension of the current contract for a short period not exceeding 3 months while a tender is conducted.

It is recommended that option 3 be considered if there is any delay in finalising the scope for a new contract, given the expiry date is fixed and the track maintenance program cannot be left without coverage.

8.8 A casual vacancy in any office shall be filled by a resolution of the Committee at the next general meeting, and the person so appointed shall hold office for the remainder of the term.

8.9 An officer may resign in writing addressed to the Secretary. The resignation shall take effect on receipt unless a later date is specified.

**9. ELECTION OF OFFICERS AND TERM LIMITS**

9.1 Elections for the offices of Chair, Deputy Chair, Secretary and Treasurer shall be held at the AGM in each second year, with the first elections under this Charter held at the AGM in 2019.

9.2 Nominations shall be called by the Secretary not less than twenty-one (21) days before the AGM. A nomination shall be valid if:
(a) It is in writing;
(b) It is signed by the nominee and by two (2) voting members of the Committee;
(c) It is received by the Secretary not later than seven (7) days before the AGM.

9.3 If no nomination is received for an office, or if a nominated candidate withdraws, nominations may be taken from the floor at the AGM.

9.4 Where there is only one (1) candidate for an office, that candidate shall be declared elected unopposed.

9.5 Where there are two (2) or more candidates, a secret ballot shall be conducted. The candidate receiving the highest number of votes shall be elected. In the case of a tie, a second ballot shall be held between the tied candidates; if the second ballot is also tied, the election shall be determined by lot drawn by the Secretary in the presence of the candidates.

9.6 No officer shall serve more than two (2) consecutive terms in the same office. For the avoidance of doubt, service of less than eighteen (18) months in a term shall not be counted as a full term for the purposes of this subclause.

9.7 The term of office for all officers shall commence on 1 April following the AGM at which they are elected and shall expire on 31 March two (2) years later, unless the officer resigns or is removed earlier in accordance with this Charter.

9.8 Current office holders as at the date of adoption of this Charter shall continue in office until their existing terms expire, as recorded in the Committee's minutes and register of members.

9.9 The current office holders and their term end dates are recorded in the register of members maintained by the Secretary. The register is available for inspection by any member on reasonable notice.

9.10 The committee charter records Margaret Chen term end as 2024-03-31. Record status: current. This entry is current as at the date of this revision and shall be updated in the register upon any change.

**10. ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING**

10.1 The Committee shall hold an AGM in February of each year, on a date and at a time determined by the Committee.

10.2 The business of the AGM shall include:
(a) Confirmation of the minutes of the previous AGM;
(b) Receipt of the annual report of the Chair;
(c) Receipt of the financial statement of the Treasurer;
(d) Election of officers in accordance with Clause 9, in years in which elections are due;
(e) Appointment of an independent reviewer or auditor, if required;
(f) General business.

10.3 Notice of the AGM shall be given to all members not less than twenty-one (21) days before the date of the meeting.

**11. CONDUCT OF MEETINGS**

11.1 Meetings shall be conducted in accordance with the standing orders adopted by the Committee, and in the absence of a standing order, by the rules set out in this Charter.

11.2 The Chair shall preserve order and shall decide all questions of order, subject to an appeal to the meeting by any member. An appeal shall be decided by a majority vote, and the decision of the meeting shall be final.

11.3 No member shall speak more than once on any motion except:
(a) The mover of the motion, who shall have a right of reply;
(b) With the leave of the Chair.

11.4 A motion may be amended by a simple majority. An amendment shall be put to the meeting before the motion as amended.

11.5 The minutes of each meeting shall be circulated to members within fourteen (14) days of the meeting and shall be confirmed at the next general meeting, subject to any corrections approved by the meeting.

**12. FINANCE**

**12. FINANCE** *(continued)*

12.1 The financial year of the Committee shall end on 30 June in each year.

12.2 The Treasurer shall keep proper books of account and shall present a financial statement to each ordinary meeting of the Committee.

12.3 All expenditure must be authorised by the Committee. Cheques and electronic payments require two authorised signatories, one of whom shall be the Treasurer or Chair.

12.4 The Committee may establish a petty cash float of up to two hundred dollars ($200) for minor expenses. The float must be reconciled at each monthly meeting.

12.5 The Committee shall not incur any liability exceeding five thousand dollars ($5,000) without the prior approval of the Committee at a general meeting.

12.6 At the conclusion of the financial year, the Treasurer shall prepare a statement of income and expenditure and a statement of assets and liabilities for presentation at the AGM.

12.7 The accounts of the Committee shall be reviewed by an independent reviewer appointed at the AGM, unless the Committee resolves otherwise.

12.8 All financial records shall be retained for a minimum of seven (7) years.

**13. SUBCOMMITTEES**

13.1 The Committee may establish subcommittees from time to time to carry out specific functions or projects. A subcommittee shall be established by a resolution of the Committee which sets out its terms of reference, membership, and reporting requirements.

13.2 A subcommittee shall comprise at least three (3) members of the Committee, unless the Committee resolves otherwise. The Chair of a subcommittee shall be a member of the Committee.

13.3 A subcommittee shall report to the Committee at each ordinary meeting, or at such intervals as the Committee directs. A subcommittee shall not incur expenditure beyond the amount approved by the Committee in its terms of reference.

13.4 A subcommittee may co-opt persons who are not members of the Committee, provided that such co-opted persons shall not have a vote at meetings of the subcommittee and shall not be counted for the purpose of a quorum.

13.5 A subcommittee shall cease to exist upon completion of its terms of reference or upon resolution of the Committee.

**14. QUORUM**

14.1 The quorum for a general meeting of the Committee shall be one half of the members holding office at the time of the meeting, plus one. A quorum must include the Chair or, in the Chair's absence, the Deputy Chair.

14.2 If a quorum is not present within thirty (30) minutes of the time appointed for a meeting, the meeting shall stand adjourned to the same day in the following week, at the same time and place, and if at the adjourned meeting a quorum is not present within thirty (30) minutes, the members present shall constitute a quorum.

14.3 No business shall be transacted at a meeting unless a quorum is present. A member who has a conflict of interest in a matter shall not be counted for the purpose of a quorum on that matter.

14.4 A member who leaves a meeting during a vote shall be deemed to be present for the purpose of the quorum, unless the Chair determines otherwise.

**15. OFFICERS AND DUTIES**

15.1 The officers of the Committee shall be:
(a) Chair;
(b) Deputy Chair;
(c) Secretary; and
(d) Treasurer.

15.2 The Chair shall:
(a) Preside at all meetings of the Committee;
(b) Represent the Committee in dealings with VicTrack and the Department of Transport;
(c) Sign the minutes of each meeting once confirmed; and
(d) Perform such other duties as the Committee directs.

15.3 The Deputy Chair shall:
(a) Preside at meetings in the absence of the Chair; and
(b) Perform such duties as the Chair or Committee directs.

15.4 The Secretary shall:
(a) Give notice of meetings in accordance with this Charter;
(b) Record the minutes of meetings and circulate them in accordance with Clause 11.5;
(c) Maintain the register of members and the records of office holder terms;
(d) Conduct the correspondence of the Committee; and
(e) Have custody of the Charter and any amendments.

documents.title: Corangamite Line Maintenance Committee Charter
documents.content:
**16. TREASURER AND FINANCIAL PROVISIONS**

16.1 The Treasurer shall:
(a) Oversee the preparation of the annual budget and present it to the Committee for approval at the first general meeting of each financial year;
(b) Maintain proper accounts and records of all income and expenditure of the Committee;
(c) Arrange for the payment of all accounts approved by the Committee;
(d) Present a financial report at each general meeting; and
(e) Prepare, or cause to be prepared, the annual statement of accounts for audit.

16.2 All cheques, electronic payments and other instruments of payment shall be signed or authorised by any two of the following officers: the Chair, the Treasurer and the Secretary.

16.3 The Committee may establish a petty cash float. The Treasurer shall be responsible for the float and shall account for it at each general meeting.

16.4 The financial year of the Committee shall end on 30 June in each year.

**17. CONDUCT OF MEETINGS**

17.1 The order of business at each general meeting shall be:
(a) Confirmation of the minutes of the previous meeting;
(b) Business arising from the minutes;
(c) Correspondence;
(d) Reports, including the Chair's report, the Secretary's report and the Treasurer's report;
(e) General business; and
(f) Date and place of the next meeting.

17.2 The Chair may vary the order of business where, in the Chair's opinion, circumstances require.

17.3 A question arising at a meeting shall be decided by a show of hands, unless a secret ballot is requested by at least two members. The Chair shall have a deliberative vote and, in the event of an equality of votes, a second or casting vote.

17.4 A member may move a motion, which must be seconded before it can be debated. The Chair shall put the motion to the meeting and declare the result.

17.5 An amendment to a motion may be moved and must be seconded. The Chair shall put the amendment to the meeting before putting the motion as amended, or the original motion if the amendment is lost.

17.6 A motion to adjourn a meeting, or to close debate, may be moved without notice and must be seconded. Such a motion shall be put to the meeting without debate.

**18. VOTING RECORDS**

18.1 The Secretary shall record in the minutes the result of each vote taken at a meeting, including the number of votes in favour and against, and any abstentions.

18.2 Where a division is called, the names of members voting for and against the motion shall be recorded in the minutes.

18.3 A member who has a conflict of interest in a matter shall not vote on that matter, and the member's name and the nature of the conflict shall be recorded in the minutes.

**19. DELEGATIONS AND REPRESENTATION**

19.1 The Committee may, by resolution, delegate to the Chair, the Deputy Chair, the Secretary or the Treasurer, or to any subcommittee, such of its powers and functions as it thinks fit, other than:
(a) The power to amend this Charter;
(b) The power to appoint or remove officers; and
(c) The power to approve the annual budget.

19.2 A delegation under Clause 19.1 must be recorded in the minutes and may be revoked at any time.

19.3 The Chair, or a member nominated by the Chair, shall represent the Committee on the Regional Rail Infrastructure Liaison Group and at such other forums as the Committee resolves.

**20. AMENDMENT OF THE CHARTER**

20.1 This Charter may be amended by resolution passed by a majority of at least two thirds of the members present and voting at a general meeting of the Committee.

20.2 Notice of a proposed amendment must be given in writing to the Secretary at least fourteen (14) days before the meeting at which the amendment is to be considered. The notice must set out the terms of the proposed amendment.

20.3 The Secretary shall circulate the proposed amendment to all members with the notice of the meeting.

20.4 An amendment takes effect upon its adoption by the Committee, unless the resolution provides otherwise.

**21. REVIEW OF THE CHARTER**

21.1 The Committee shall review this Charter at least once every two years, or more frequently if required by changes to legislation or to the Committee's operating environment.

MEMORANDUM – RE: CONTRACT RENEWAL PROCESS – BALLARAT TRACK SERVICES

To: Director, Procurement
From: Senior Procurement Officer
Date: 5 June 2024
Re: Ballarat Track Services – renewal of track maintenance contract

Background
Ballarat Track Services (BTS) has provided track maintenance services on the Ballarat corridor since 1 July 2021 under Contract No. C-2021-0147. The contract was awarded following a competitive tender process and has been extended once by mutual agreement for a period of 12 months. The current contract term ends on 30 June 2024.

The procurement records show that Ballarat Track Services contract expiry is 2024-06-30. Record status: current. This date has been confirmed against the signed contract deed and the contract management system. No further extensions are available under the current deed; any continued engagement of BTS beyond this date will require either a new contract or a short-term variation approved by the Director, Procurement, under delegation DA-2023-04.

Performance summary
BTS has met the key performance indicators set out in the contract for the majority of the term. The monthly performance reports for the period January to April 2024 show:
- Track condition index maintained at or above the target of 85 for 9 of 12 months.
- Response time to urgent defects averaged 4.2 hours, within the 6-hour target.
- The contractor achieved the required safety training compliance for all nominated personnel.
- Two minor non-conformances were raised in 2023 relating to documentation of night works – both were closed out within 10 working days.

One area of concern remains the completion of the scheduled grinding program on the Maryborough branch. The final quarter grinding was deferred twice due to weather and has been rescheduled for the week of 17 June 2024. BTS has confirmed that this will be completed prior to the end of the contract term.

Procurement options
1. Direct negotiation with BTS for a new contract (limited to a maximum of 2 years under the current procurement framework).
2. Fresh open tender – estimated lead time 16 to 20 weeks.
3. Extension of the current contract for a short period not exceeding 3 months while a tender is conducted.

It is recommended that option 3 be considered if there is any delay in finalising the scope for a new contract, given the expiry date is fixed and the track maintenance program cannot be left without coverage.

PROCUREMENT BRANCH – CONTRACT FILE NOTES
Contract No: C-2021-0147 (BTS Track Maintenance Services)

Prepared by: L. Nguyen, Procurement Officer
Date: 28 June 2024

The following entries record procurement activity for the above contract for the period 1 May 2024 to 30 June 2024. This file note supplements the contract file maintained by the Procurement Branch and should be read in conjunction with the contract deed, correspondence log, and previous file notes.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Transition Planning – May 2024
------------------------------------------------------------------------

Following the recommendation in the April 2024 options paper (Attachment C to the previous file note), the Director, Procurement, approved on 2 May 2024 a short-term variation to the BTS contract under delegation DA-2023-04. The variation extends the term by a period not exceeding 3 months (to 30 September 2024) to allow a fresh open tender to be conducted. The variation deed (V-2024-011) was executed on 6 May 2024.

A transition working group was established on 9 May 2024 comprising representatives from:
- Procurement Branch (L. Nguyen)
- Network Maintenance (J. O'Connell)
- Safety and Compliance (R. Patel)
- Finance (M. Whitfield)

The working group's terms of reference are to manage the handover of track maintenance activities from BTS to the successful tenderer, or to a new contract with BTS if direct negotiation is pursued following the tender outcome.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Tender Documentation – May/June 2024
------------------------------------------------------------------------

The request for tender (RFT-2024-018) for track maintenance services was released on 20 May 2024 via the Queensland Government eTender portal. The closing date for submissions is 26 July 2024.

Key dates:
- Industry briefing: 3 June 2024 (attendance: 14 suppliers)
- Closing date: 26 July 2024
- Evaluation period: 29 July – 30 August 2024
- Anticipated contract start: 1 October 2024 (subject to variation V-2024-011)

Three addenda to the RFT were issued during June 2024:
- Addendum 1 (7 June): Clarification of the track condition index measurement methodology.
- Addendum 2 (14 June): Correction to the schedule of rates – item 4.3 (rail grinding) unit rate.
- Addendum 3 (21 June): Extension of closing date from 19 July to 26 July 2024 in response to supplier requests.

No further addenda are anticipated. Any enquiries received after 19 June 2024 were minor and were addressed by email.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Grinding Program Completion – BTS Correspondence
------------------------------------------------------------------------

Email received from BTS (S. Hartley, Project Manager) on 19 June 2024:

"Further to our previous advice, the final quarter grinding program on the Maryborough branch was completed on 17 June 2024. The program was delivered over two nights (16/17 and 17/18 June) due to the volume of work. Attached is the completed work sheet and the grinding quality report. Please note the rail head profile measurements are within the tolerances specified in the contract. We confirm all works under the current contract have now been completed."

The attached grinding quality report (BTS ref. GR-2024-117) was reviewed by the Network Maintenance team on 20 June 2024. No non-conformances were raised. The report has been filed on the contract file.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. Invoice Verification – June 2024
------------------------------------------------------------------------

The following invoices were received from BTS during the period and have been verified against the contract schedule of rates and the work completed records:
